title.en: Volume 365 Biographies 152: Jue Luo Bao Xing, Zong Shijingzheng, Zong Shixien, Chen Guanjun, Zhuo Bingtian
title.raw: 卷365 列傳一百五十二 觉罗宝兴 宗室敬徴 宗室禧恩 陈官俊 卓秉恬

sentences.zh: 列傳一百五十二

translations.literal: Biography 152
translations.idiomatic: Biography 152

sentences.zh: 覺羅寶興宗室敬徵宗室禧恩陳官俊卓秉恬

translations.literal: Jueluo Bao Xing, imperial clansman Jingzheng, imperial clansman Xien, Chen Guanjun, and Zhuo Bingtian
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Bao Xing, the imperial clansmen Jingzheng and Xien, Chen Guanjun, and Zhuo Bingtian

sentences.zh: 覺羅寶興，字獻山，隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Jueluo Bao Xing, styled Xianshan, belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Bao Xing, courtesy name Xianshan, was registered in the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Jiaqing 15 (1810), entered the Hanlin as a probationer academician, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷少詹事，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and entered permanent duty in the Imperial Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and was assigned to regular duty in the Imperial Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 十八年，仁宗幸熱河，林清逆黨突入禁城，寶興散直，至東華門與賊遇，急入告警。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Emperor Renzong went to Rehe; Lin Qing's rebel faction burst into the Forbidden City; Bao Xing was off duty, reached the East Flowery Gate, met the bandits, and hurried in to raise the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813), while Emperor Renzong was at Rehe, followers of the rebel Lin Qing broke into the Forbidden City. Bao Xing happened to be off rotation; at the East Flowery Gate he ran into the assailants and rushed inside to sound the warning.

sentences.zh: 宣宗方在上書房，聞警戒備，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor was just then in the Imperial Lecture Hall; hearing the alarm he ordered precautions, and the bandits could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Xuanzong was in the Imperial Lecture Hall at the time; on hearing the alarm he put the defenses in order, and the rebels were unable to carry out their plot.

sentences.zh: 上還京，擢寶興內閣學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital he promoted Bao Xing to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Beijing, Bao Xing was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以事忤旨，詔斥寶興不學，降大理寺卿，罷直書房。

translations.literal: On account of a matter that offended the imperial will, an edict denounced Bao Xing as unlearned, demoted him to President of the Court of Judicial Review, and removed him from duty in the Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the throne over a particular affair; an edict castigated him as poorly educated, reduced him to President of the Court of Judicial Review, and stripped him of his Lecture Hall posting.

sentences.zh: 复坐部刊科場條例誤「高宗」為「高祖」，降二級調用。

translations.literal: Again, because in the ministry's printed examination regulations "Gaozong" had been misprinted as "Gaozu," he was demoted two ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished again when regulations on the examination grounds published by his ministry misprinted "Gaozong" as "Gaozu"; he was lowered two ranks and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 尋予三等侍衛，充吐魯番領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was given the third-rank guardsman's post and appointed leading commissioner to Turfan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a third-class imperial guardsman and sent as chief commissioner to Turfan.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，召為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was recalled as Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 (1822) he was recalled to serve as Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 復因事降通政司參議，歷左副都御史、兵部侍郎，出為泰宁鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Again on account of affairs he was demoted to participating secretary of the Office of Transmission, then served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, and went out as regional commander at Taining garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again over another matter to participating secretary of the Office of Transmission, later held the posts of Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, and was sent out as garrison commander of Taining.

sentences.zh: 八年，授理籓院侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 he became Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and was then moved to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 迭命偕戶部尚書王鼎察治長蘆、兩淮鹽務，籌議整頓，詳王鼎傳。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he was ordered together with Minister of Revenue Wang Ding to investigate and rectify the Changlu and Liang-Huai salt administrations and to deliberate on reform; details are given in Wang Ding's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly assigned with Wang Ding, Minister of Revenue, to inspect and reform the Changlu and Two Huai salt monopolies; the full account appears in Wang Ding's biography.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為吉林將軍，疏言：「松花江西岸、輝發河北岸舊例封禁，其餘閒曠山場均設卡倫，惟許兵丁打捕牲畜，以備貢品。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as General of Jilin and memorialized: "Along the west bank of the Songhua River and the north bank of the Huifa River prohibitions were customary; elsewhere vacant hills and pastures all had barrier stations, and only soldiers were permitted to hunt and take livestock for tribute goods."
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 10 he was appointed general of Jilin and submitted a memorial: "The west bank of the Songhua and the north bank of the Huifa had long been closed to entry by statute; other idle hills and pastures were posted with cordon stations, allowing only garrison troops to hunt game for tribute purposes."

sentences.zh: 民人無照，私出挖蓡斫木者，查拏治罪。

translations.literal: Commoners who went out without permits to dig ginseng or cut timber were to be seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians who ventured out without licenses to dig ginseng or fell timber were to be apprehended and punished.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「伯都訥珠爾山荒田先後開墾五千二百六十二晌，其租息請自道光十五年為始，以其半分賞兵丁，半存備報修工程。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "On the wasteland of Bodunezhu'er Mountain 5,262 shang had been opened to cultivation in succession; please have the rent begin from the fifteenth year of Daoguang, half to be distributed as rewards to the soldiers and half kept in reserve for reporting and repair projects."
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "On the wasteland of Bodunezhu'er Mountain, 5,262 shang had been brought under the plow in stages; he asked that rents commence from Daoguang 15, with half distributed to the troops as bounty and half set aside for upkeep and repair works."

sentences.zh: 此外尚有可墾荒地五萬六千餘晌，作為官荒，將來奏請招佃徵租。

translations.literal: Besides this there remained more than fifty-six thousand shang of land that could still be reclaimed, to be treated as official wasteland and later memorialized for soliciting tenants and collecting rent.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, more than fifty-six thousand shang of reclaimable wasteland should be held as state land and, in due course, opened to tenants with rents levied by memorial.

sentences.zh: 烏拉涼水泉已墾七萬三千九百餘晌，請撥二道河東二萬晌，以七成給烏拉總管衙門，三成給協領衙門，資為津貼。

translations.literal: At Wula Liangshuiquan 73,900-odd shang had already been reclaimed; he requested allotting twenty thousand shang east of Erdao River, seventy percent to the Wula commandant's yamen and thirty percent to the assistant commandant's yamen as allowances.
translations.idiomatic: At Wula Liangshuiquan more than 73,900 shang were already under cultivation; he proposed allotting twenty thousand shang east of the Erdao River—seventy percent to the Wula commandant's office and thirty percent to the assistant commandant's office—as supplementary stipends.

sentences.zh: 餘未墾地五萬三千餘晌，亦作官荒。

translations.literal: The remaining unreclaimed land of more than fifty-three thousand shang was also to be treated as official wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining unreclaimed tract of more than fifty-three thousand shang was likewise to be reserved as state wasteland.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " The court approved all.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 調盛京，又調成都。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Mukden, then again to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Mukden and later to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署四川總督，逾年實授。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he served as acting Governor-General of Sichuan; the following year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 17 he acted as governor-general of Sichuan and received the substantive post the year after.

sentences.zh: 時馬邊、越巂邊外夷匪數出為患。

translations.literal: At that time beyond the borders of Mabian and Yuexi barbarian bandits repeatedly came forth and caused trouble.
translations.idiomatic: At that time non-Han raiders beyond the Mabian and Yuexi frontiers were raiding with increasing frequency.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏言：「禦邊之策，不外剿、撫、防三者，撫之之道，在施於平時，斷無失利之後轉而就撫之理。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized: "Policies for defending the frontier are nothing beyond suppression, pacification, and defense; the way of pacification lies in applying it in normal times—there is absolutely no principle of turning to pacification only after defeat."
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 he memorialized: "Frontier policy comes down to suppression, conciliation, and defense. Conciliation must be practiced in peacetime; there is no sense in resorting to it only after military setbacks."

sentences.zh: 比來勞師糜餉，迄無成功。

translations.literal: Recently troops have been exhausted and provisions wasted, yet success has not been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Recent campaigns had worn out the army and drained the treasury without achieving results.

sentences.zh: 為今計者，以修邊防為急務，陳防邊五事：一、增兵額，請於馬邊增兵千二百，雷波、普安、安阜、越巂、寧越各增兵八百，瓘邊、屏山各增兵四百；

translations.literal: For the present plan, strengthening frontier defense should be the urgent task; he set forth five matters for border defense: first, increase troop quotas—request at Mabian an increase of 1,200 troops, at Leibo, Pu'an, Anfu, Yuexi, and Ningyue each 800, and at Qianbian and Pingshan each 400;
translations.idiomatic: His immediate proposal was to make frontier fortification the priority. He outlined five measures: first, raise troop quotas—1,200 more at Mabian, 800 each at Leibo, Pu'an, Anfu, Yuexi, and Ningyue, and 400 each at Qianbian and Pingshan;

sentences.zh: 一、改營製，請以綏定協副將移駐馬邊廳城，游擊、都司以下各增設移駐有差；

translations.literal: second, reform the garrison system—request that the Suiding brigade deputy commander move his headquarters to Mabian subprefecture city, and that brigade colonels, regimental colonels, and ranks below each be added and relocated in varying degrees;
translations.idiomatic: second, reorganize the garrison structure—station the Suiding brigade deputy commander at Mabian city and redistribute brigade colonels, regimental colonels, and subordinate officers to new posts as needed;

sentences.zh: 一、築碉堡，飭各廳縣因地制宜，多修堡寨，責令各集團練，官給抬砲，督率教演，擇要隘築砲台，增設大砲；

translations.literal: third, build blockhouses and forts—order each subprefecture and county according to local conditions to repair many stockades and forts, charge each community militia, supply swivel guns from the government, supervise training and drill, select strategic passes to build batteries, and add heavy cannon;
translations.idiomatic: third, build blockhouses and stockades—have each district adapt works to local terrain, organize community militia, issue swivel guns from official stores, supervise drill, erect batteries at key passes, and deploy additional artillery;

sentences.zh: 一、定期巡閱，歲春夏之交，建昌道赴越巂、瓘邊，永寧道赴馬邊、雷波、屏山，週曆巡閱各一次，秋冬責成提督與建昌總兵分赴巡行察勘邊隘；

translations.literal: fourth, institute regular inspections—between spring and summer each year the Jianchang circuit intendant should go to Yuexi and Qianbian, the Yongning circuit intendant to Mabian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each making one full round of inspection; in autumn and winter the provincial commander-in-chief and the Jianchang regional commander should be charged to go separately on patrol to examine frontier passes;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, schedule regular inspections—each spring the Jianchang intendant would tour Yuexi and Qianbian, the Yongning intendant Mabian, Leibo, and Pingshan; in autumn and winter the provincial commander and Jianchang regional commander would divide frontier reconnaissance between them;

sentences.zh: 一、優獎邊吏，馬邊、越巂兩廳同知，請三年俸滿，以題調選缺知府升補。

translations.literal: fifth, reward frontier officials favorably—the two subprefectural vice prefects of Mabian and Yuexi, request that after three years' salary completion they be promoted by special nomination to selected prefect vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, reward frontier officials—the vice prefects of Mabian and Yuexi should, after three years in post, be elevated by special nomination to substantive prefectural appointments.

sentences.zh: 」疏下議行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred for deliberation and carried out.

sentences.zh: 言官論奏四川提督應如湖南例，半年駐越巂等處。

translations.literal: Censorial officials memorialized that the Sichuan provincial commander-in-chief should follow the Hunan precedent and reside half the year at Yuexi and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued that the Sichuan commander-in-chief, following the Hunan precedent, should spend half the year stationed in Yuexi and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 寶興議：「馬邊、越巂相距遼遠，請於春秋夷匪出沒之時，提督往駐馬邊、瓘邊、雷波三廳，建昌總兵往駐越巂、寧越。

translations.literal: Bao Xing deliberated: "Mabian and Yuexi are far apart; request that in spring and autumn when barbarian bandits appear and disappear, the provincial commander go to station at the three subprefectures of Mabian, Qianbian, and Leibo, and the Jianchang regional commander go to station at Yuexi and Ningyue."
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xing countered: "Mabian and Yuexi lie far apart. In spring and autumn, when raiders are most active, the commander-in-chief should station at Mabian, Qianbian, and Leibo, and the Jianchang regional commander at Yuexi and Ningyue."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「越巂邊防以大路為重，麥子營、利濟站均應增駐弁兵，乾溝諸汛應酌量移撤，分設於馬日槓諸處。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "For Yuexi frontier defense the main road is crucial; Maiziying and Lijizhan both should have increased garrison of officers and troops; the various posts at Qiangou should be suitably moved and withdrawn and redeployed at Marigang and other places."
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "Yuexi defense hinges on the main road. Maiziying and Lijizhan need reinforced garrisons, while posts at Qiangou should be thinned and redeployed to Marigang and similar points."

sentences.zh: 越巂、寧越兩營相距頗遠，聲勢不能相及。

translations.literal: The two garrisons of Yuexi and Ningyue were quite far apart and their strength could not support each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuexi and Ningyue garrisons lay too far apart for mutual support.

sentences.zh: 前請以建昌左營游擊移駐大菩薩地，遠在寧越之東，而越巂營參將復與游擊不相統屬。

translations.literal: Previously it was requested that the Jianchang Left Brigade colonel move to Dapusa, far to the east of Ningyue, while the Yuexi garrison brigade general was again not in the same chain of command as the colonel.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier proposal had moved the Jianchang Left Brigade colonel to Dapusa, far east of Ningyue, yet left him outside the command of the Yuexi garrison brigade general.

sentences.zh: 請越巂、寧越適中之界牌樓，以建昌鎮右營都司移駐，專管麥子營、利濟站兩汛。

translations.literal: He requested that at Jiepailou, midway between Yuexi and Ningyue, the Jianchang garrison Right Brigade regimental colonel be moved to station and be charged solely with the two posts of Maiziying and Lijizhan.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed stationing the Jianchang Right Brigade regimental colonel at Jiepailou, midway between Yuexi and Ningyue, with sole responsibility for Maiziying and Lijizhan.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " The court approved all.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 先是寶興以馬邊諸廳縣增設防兵，籌議邊防經費，請按糧津貼，計可徵銀百萬兩，以三十萬為初設防兵之需。

translations.literal: Earlier Bao Xing, because of increased frontier troops in the Mabian subprefectures and counties, deliberated on frontier defense funds and requested a grain surcharge allowance, calculating that one million taels of silver could be levied, with three hundred thousand for the initial needs of the new frontier troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, to fund new garrisons in the Mabian districts, Bao Xing had proposed a grain surcharge, estimating a levy of one million taels—three hundred thousand for initial troop costs.

sentences.zh: 每歲經費，即以餘銀七十萬兩生息，置田供支。

translations.literal: Annual expenses were to use the remaining seven hundred thousand taels to earn interest and purchase land for support.
translations.idiomatic: Annual upkeep was to come from investing the remaining seven hundred thousand taels and purchasing land whose rents would cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 上以津貼病民，撥部帑銀百萬。

translations.literal: The emperor considered the surcharge harmful to the people and allocated one million taels from the ministry treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged the surcharge too burdensome on the populace and allotted one million taels from the central treasury instead.

sentences.zh: 翰林院侍讀學士王炳瀛奏：「四川前買義田，遍​​及百餘州縣，若更以數十萬帑銀於各州縣買田收租，膏腴將盡歸公產。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy Reader Wang Bingying memorialized: "Sichuan had previously purchased charity fields extending to more than a hundred prefectures and counties; if further hundreds of thousands of taels from the treasury were used to buy land and collect rent in each prefecture and county, the best fields would all pass into public ownership."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Reader Wang Bingying warned: "Sichuan already held charity estates in more than a hundred districts; spending hundreds of thousands more in treasury silver to buy land for rent across the province would concentrate the best soil in state hands."

sentences.zh: 請限於四廳近邊地收買，安置屯防。

translations.literal: He requested limiting purchases to land near the four subprefectures on the frontier and settling garrison colonization defense.
translations.idiomatic: He urged limiting purchases to land near the four frontier subprefectures and using it to settle garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 」下寶興妥議，疏言：「邊防完竣，用銀二十二萬兩有奇，以三十七萬發鹽茶各商，歲得息三萬七千餘兩，足敷增設練勇餉械之需。

translations.literal: " The matter was sent down to Bao Xing for proper deliberation; he memorialized: "Frontier defense works were completed, using a little more than 220,000 taels of silver; 370,000 were lent to salt and tea merchants, yielding over 37,000 taels interest yearly, sufficient to cover pay and arms for the added trained braves."
translations.idiomatic: " The court referred the matter to Bao Xing, who reported: "Frontier works cost just over 220,000 taels. He proposed lending 370,000 to salt and tea merchants at interest—more than 37,000 taels a year—enough to pay the new militia and equip them."

sentences.zh: 餘銀四十萬，聽部撥別用。

translations.literal: The remaining 400,000 taels of silver were left to the ministry to allocate for other uses.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining 400,000 taels were to be disposed of by the ministry as it saw fit.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷買田議，二十一年，拜文淵閣大學士，留四川總督任。

translations.literal: " The plan to buy land was then abandoned; in the twenty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity while retaining the post of Governor-General of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: " The land-purchase scheme was dropped. In Daoguang 21 he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity while remaining governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時大學士琦善、協辦大學士伊里布相繼罷，在朝滿洲大臣鮮當上意，故有是授。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Qishan and Associate Grand Secretary Yilibu had been dismissed in succession; among Manchu ministers at court few pleased the emperor, hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Qishan and Associate Grand Secretary Yilibu had just been removed in succession, and few Manchu ministers at court enjoyed the emperor's confidence—hence this appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，入覲，命留京管理刑部，充上書房總師傅，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he came to audience and was ordered to remain in the capital to administer the Ministry of Justice, serve as chief tutor of the Imperial Lecture Hall, and concurrently hold the post of Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 26 he attended court and was ordered to remain in Beijing to head the Ministry of Justice, serve as chief tutor of the Imperial Lecture Hall, and concurrently serve as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十八年元旦，加恩年老諸臣，加太保。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the twenty-eighth year, in extending grace to aged ministers, he was given the honorary title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Daoguang 28, as part of a grace for senior officials, he received the honorary rank of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒，年七十二，諡文莊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died, aged seventy-two; his posthumous title was Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month at the age of seventy-two and was given the posthumous name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 宗室敬徵，隸鑲白旗，肅親王永錫子。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Jingzheng belonged to the Bordered White Banner and was a son of Prince Su Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Jingzheng was registered in the Bordered White Banner and was a son of Prince Su Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，封輔國公，授頭等侍衛，兼委散秩大臣、副都統。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he was enfeoffed as Duke of the Second Rank, appointed first-rank guardsman, and concurrently entrusted as minister without regular rank and vice president of the Bordered Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he was created Duke of the Second Rank, made a first-class imperial guardsman, and concurrently entrusted as a minister without regular rank and vice president of the Bordered Banner.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授內閣學士，兼鑾儀使，充總族長。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently Director of Imperial Ceremonial, and charged as chief clan head.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 he became Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently Director of Imperial Ceremonial, and was appointed chief head of the clan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，失察宗室海康等習紅陽教，褫職，謫居盛京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, for failure to detect imperial clansmen Haikang and others practicing the Hongyang sect, he was stripped of office and banished to reside at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 he was dismissed for failing to detect clansmen such as Haikang practicing the Hongyang sect and was exiled to Mukden.

sentences.zh: 尋予四等侍衛，乾清門行走。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was given the fourth-rank guardsman's post and permission to attend at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as a fourth-class guardsman with attendance at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 道光初，累遷工部侍郎，授內務府大臣，調戶部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Works, appointed Minister of the Imperial Household, and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he rose to Vice Minister of Works, became Minister of the Imperial Household, and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕尚書王鼎察治長蘆鹽務，奏定歸補帑課章程，詳王鼎傳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Minister Wang Ding he investigated and rectified the Changlu salt administration and memorialized fixed regulations for restoring treasury salt duties; details are given in Wang Ding's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 he joined Minister Wang Ding in reforming the Changlu salt monopoly and framed regulations for restoring treasury revenues; see Wang Ding's biography.

sentences.zh: 十二年，南河奸民陳堂等盜決於家灣官堤，命偕尚書硃士彥往勘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on the Southern River ruffians Chen Tang and others illicitly breaching the official dike at Yujiawan, he was ordered together with Minister Zhu Shiyan to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12, after ruffians led by Chen Tang illicitly breached the official dike at Yujiawan on the Southern River, he was sent with Minister Zhu Shiyan to inspect the damage.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「諸口已合，壩下尚未閉氣，間有蟄陷。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The breaches had all been closed, but below the dam the seal had not yet set and there were occasional subsidence collapses."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "The breaches had been closed, but the seal below the dam had not fully set and there were occasional sinkholes."

sentences.zh: 陳堂等聽從逸犯陳端糾眾，以為從例問擬，疏防各官遣戍。

translations.literal: Chen Tang and others had obeyed the escaped convict Chen Duan in gathering a crowd; they were sentenced under the statute for followers; officials negligent in defense were sent to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang and his accomplices had followed the fugitive Chen Duan in raising a mob; they were sentenced as accessories, and negligent officials were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 通判張懋祖賠修壩工不實，罰賠枷號。

translations.literal: Assistant Prefect Zhang Maozu's compensation for dike repair was not genuine; he was fined compensation and placed in the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant prefect Zhang Maozu had falsified his reimbursement for dike repairs and was fined and placed in the cangue.

sentences.zh: 覆勘湖河各工，請擇要興修，高堰、山盱卑矮石工，分年改砌碎石；

translations.literal: On re-inspection of the various works on lake and river, he requested selecting important items for construction; the low stone works at Gaoyan and Shanxu should be rebuilt with rubble stone over successive years;
translations.idiomatic: On reinspection of lake and river works he proposed priority repairs: the low stone revetments at Gaoyan and Shanxu should be rebuilt in rubble over several years;

sentences.zh: 信壩補還石工，智壩、仁河、義河壩改修石底；

translations.literal: at Xinba restore the stone works; at Zhiba, Renhe, and Yihe dams rebuild the stone foundations;
translations.idiomatic: restore stone work at Xinba; rebuild the stone foundations at Zhiba, Renhe, and Yihe dams;

sentences.zh: 里河福興閘塌卸，急築；

translations.literal: on the inner river the Fuxing sluice had collapsed and should be urgently rebuilt;
translations.idiomatic: urgently rebuild the collapsed Fuxing sluice on the inner channel;

sentences.zh: 揚河西岸加高磚工，改拋碎石。

translations.literal: on the west bank of the Yang River raise the brick works and change to dumping rubble stone.
translations.idiomatic: raise the brick revetment on the west bank of the Yang River and replace it with dumped rubble.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " The court approved all.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 又會同兩江總督陶澍議定淮鹽票引兼行，言官所論官票運私、侵礙暢岸、爭佔馬頭三者皆可無慮，詔如原議行。

translations.literal: He also joined Governor-General Tao Shu of the Two Jiangs in fixing the joint operation of Huai salt tickets and salt certificates; the three points censorial officials raised—official tickets used for private transport, encroachment on flourishing banks, and seizing wharves—could all be disregarded, and an edict ordered implementation as originally proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked with Tao Shu, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, on the combined Huai salt ticket-and-certificate system. Memorialists had warned of official tickets used for smuggling, harm to thriving salt banks, and seizure of wharves; Jingzheng judged these concerns unfounded, and the court ordered the original plan carried out.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 14 he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎吳椿勘浙江海塘，疏言：「念裡亭至尖山柴工尚資禦溜，石塘仍當修整，鎮海及戴家橋汛議改竹簍，塊石不如條石坦水舊法為堅實。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister Wu Chun he investigated the Zhejiang seawall and memorialized: "From Nianliting to Jianshan the fascine works still help resist scour; the stone seawall should still be repaired; at Zhenhai and Daijiaqiao posts it was proposed to change to bamboo crates, but block stone is not as solid as the old method of strip stone for level water."
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Minister Wu Chun he inspected the Zhejiang seawall and reported: "Fascine works from Nianliting to Jianshan still help break the current; the stone seawall needs repair. Proposals to use bamboo crates at Zhenhai and Daijiaqiao were weaker than the older strip-stone revetment."

sentences.zh: 烏龍廟以東，冬工暫緩。

translations.literal: East of Wulongmiao, winter works were temporarily deferred.
translations.idiomatic: East of Wulong Temple, winter construction could wait.

sentences.zh: 」回京，擢兵部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: " On return to the capital he was promoted to Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: " On returning to the capital he was promoted to Minister of War and then transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以孝穆皇后、孝慎皇后梓宮奉安龍泉峪，諏日不慎，罷尚書、都統，仍充內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because in installing the coffins of Empress Xiaomu and Empress Xiaoshen at Longquanyu the auspicious day had been chosen carelessly, he was dismissed as minister and banner commander but still retained as Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15, after an inauspicious date was chosen for installing the coffins of Empresses Xiaomu and Xiaoshen at Longquan Valley, he was stripped of his ministerial and banner-command posts but kept on at the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 十六年，署戶部侍郎，累遷工部尚書，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as acting Vice Minister of Revenue, was promoted in succession to Minister of Works, and concurrently held the post of banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 16 he acted as Vice Minister of Revenue, rose to Minister of Works, and concurrently commanded a banner.

sentences.zh: 東河總督栗毓美多用磚工，御史李蓴言其不便，命敬徵偕蓴往勘。

translations.literal: Eastern River Governor-General Li Yumei made much use of brick works; Censor Li Chun said this was inconvenient, and Jingzheng was ordered to go with Chun to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern River governor-general Li Yumei favored brick revetments; Censor Li Chun objected, and Jingzheng was sent with him to inspect.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「已辦磚工尚屬整齊，輿論謂保灘護崖可資其力。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The brick works already completed are still in good order, and public opinion says they can help protect beaches and banks."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Completed brick works were still sound, and local opinion held they helped protect beaches and banks."

sentences.zh: 水深溜急之處，不及埽工鞏固，搶辦險工，未可深恃。

translations.literal: Where water was deep and currents swift they were not as secure as fascine works; for emergency repair of dangerous works they could not be deeply relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In deep, fast water they were less secure than fascine bundles, and for emergency repairs they could not be fully trusted.

sentences.zh: 請停止燒磚，改辦碎石。

translations.literal: He requested stopping brick firing and changing to rubble stone works.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended halting brick production and switching to rubble revetments.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 he was moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，南河揚河漫口，水由灌河入海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year on the Southern River the Yang River breached its banks and water entered the sea through the Guan River.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 the Yang River on the Southern River broke its banks and discharged into the sea through the Guan River.

sentences.zh: 有議即改新河，河督麟慶以河流未定，遽難決議，命敬徵偕尚書廖鴻荃往勘。

translations.literal: Some proposed immediately shifting to the new river course; River Governor Lin Qing said the river's course was not yet fixed and a hasty decision was difficult, and Jingzheng was ordered together with Minister Liao Hongquan to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged an immediate shift to the new channel; river governor Lin Qing argued the stream was still unsettled and no quick decision was possible. Jingzheng was dispatched with Minister Liao Hongquan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「改河之議，在因勢利導。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The proposal to shift the river lies in following the terrain advantageously."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Redirecting the river means working with the terrain, not against it."

sentences.zh: 今查灌河海口至蕭莊口門三百六十餘裡。

translations.literal: Now on investigation from the Guan River estuary to the Xiaozhuang mouth it is more than 360 li.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection showed more than 360 li from the Guan River estuary to the Xiaozhuang outlet.

sentences.zh: 新河正溜，由六塘出達灌口，其下游東北一百十里，滔滔直注。

translations.literal: The new river's main current, exiting through Liutang to reach the Guan mouth, for 110 li downstream to the northeast poured straight in torrent.
translations.idiomatic: The new main current left through Liutang for the Guan mouth and ran northeast for 110 li in a straight, roaring flood.

sentences.zh: 惟當潮漲時，黃水相逼，壅閼不前，而上游自口門至響水口二百餘裡，支流忽分忽合，必須兩岸築堤束水，方免汎濫。

translations.literal: Only when the tide rose did the Yellow water press upon it and block progress; upstream from the mouth to Xiangshuikou for more than 200 li branch streams suddenly divided and joined—dikes must be built on both banks to confine the water before flooding could be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: At high tide Yellow River water pressed in and stalled the flow. Upstream, from the mouth to Xiangshuikou for more than 200 li, channels split and rejoined unpredictably; only dikes on both banks could confine the water and prevent flooding.

sentences.zh: 計工長三百餘裡，經費難籌。

translations.literal: The works would total more than 300 li in length and funds would be hard to raise.
translations.idiomatic: Works would stretch more than 300 li—funding would be hard to secure.

sentences.zh: 且中河運道為黃流橫截，不得不移塘灌運。

translations.literal: Moreover the Middle River transport route was cut across by the Yellow current and transport had to be shifted from the Grand Canal to the Guan River.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yellow River water cut across the Middle River transport route, forcing grain traffic from the Grand Canal onto the Guan.

sentences.zh: 清水本弱，仍恃借黃以濟。

translations.literal: Clear water was inherently weak and still relied on borrowing Yellow water to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Clear water was already weak and still depended on Yellow River water to keep moving.

sentences.zh: 空船引轉需時，重運更形艱滯。

translations.literal: Empty boats required time to turn and tow; heavy transport became even more difficult and slow.
translations.idiomatic: Empty barges needed long turns; laden convoys would move even more slowly.

sentences.zh: 是移塘乃權宜之計，常年行之，恐妨運道。

translations.literal: Thus shifting transport was an expedient measure; practiced year-round it would likely harm the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting the route was an emergency measure; making it permanent would likely cripple the canal.

sentences.zh: 舊黃河自蕭莊迄舊海口四百二十餘裡，尾閭寬暢。

translations.literal: The old Yellow River from Xiaozhuang to the old estuary was more than 420 li, with a broad and open outlet.
translations.idiomatic: The old Yellow River course from Xiaozhuang to the former mouth ran more than 420 li with a broad, open outlet.

sentences.zh: 自漫口斷流，河身益淤。

translations.literal: Since the breach cut off flow, the river channel silted ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Since the breach had cut the flow, the channel had silted heavily.

sentences.zh: 若挽歸故道，堵口挑河，共費五六百萬，較改河築堤撙節實多。

translations.literal: If the river were drawn back to the old course, blocking the breach and dredging the channel would cost five or six million altogether—far more economical than shifting the river and building dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Returning the river to its old course—sealing the breach and dredging—would cost five or six million taels but would save far more than redirecting the river and building new dikes.

sentences.zh: 請定明歲春融興工，俟軍船回空後築壩合龍。

translations.literal: He requested fixing work to begin when ice melted the following spring and, after grain transport ships returned empty, building the dam to close the dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed starting work after the spring thaw the following year and closing the breach with a cofferdam once the grain fleet had returned empty.

sentences.zh: 」詔如議行。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered implementation as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the plan carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, as Minister of Revenue, he was made Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Associate Grand Secretary while serving as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，偕侍郎何汝霖赴南河勘工，又赴河南察視中河廳漫口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, together with Vice Minister He Rulin he went to the Southern River to inspect works and again went to Henan to examine the breach at the Middle River office.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 he joined Vice Minister He Rulin to inspect Southern River works and then went to Henan to survey the Middle River breach.

sentences.zh: 疏陳築壩挑河工費需銀五百十八萬兩，較祥符工費為節省，允之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that building the dam and dredging the river would require 5.18 million taels of silver—more economical than the Xiangfu project costs—and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that sealing the breach and dredging would cost 5.18 million taels, less than the Xiangfu works, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，奏：「河南下北河廳廟工，乃北岸七廳適中之所，河臣宜常年駐此，便於控制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized: "The Miaogong works of the Henan Lower North River office are the central point among the seven offices on the north bank; the river official should reside here year-round for convenient control."
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 he submitted: "The Miaogong site of the Henan Lower North River office lies midway among the seven north-bank districts; the river commissioner should keep his headquarters there year-round for effective control."

sentences.zh: 」詔河督每於伏汛前移駐廟工，立冬後仍回濟寧。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the river governor to move to Miaogong before the summer flood season each year and return to Jining after the Start of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the river governor to station at Miaogong before the summer flood season and return to Jining after winter set in.

sentences.zh: 尋坐濫保駐藏大臣孟保，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for indiscriminately recommending the Tibet resident minister Meng Bao, he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to grand secretary for recklessly recommending Meng Bao as resident minister in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复授工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 又坐濫保科布多參贊大臣果勒明阿，褫職。

translations.literal: Again, for indiscriminately recommending the Kobdo assistant resident minister Guoleming'a, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed again for improperly recommending Guoleming'a as assistant resident minister at Kobdo.

sentences.zh: 三十年，署正白旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he served as acting vice president of the Plain White Banner Manchu division.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 he acted as vice president of the Plain White Banner Manchu division.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，卒，詔念前勞，予一品銜，依尚書例賜卹，諡文★。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he died; an edict recalled his former service, granted him the first rank, bestowed condolence payments according to the ministerial precedent, and gave the posthumous title Wenqin (the text's final character is damaged).
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianfeng 1. The throne honored his past service with first rank, ministerial funeral rites, and the posthumous name Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 子恆恩，左副都御史；

translations.literal: His son Heng'en was Left Vice Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng'en served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 孫盛昱，自有傳。

translations.literal: his grandson Shengyu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: his grandson Shengyu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宗室禧恩，字仲蕃，隸正藍旗，睿親王淳穎子。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Xien, styled Zhongfan, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner and was a son of Prince Rui Chunying.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Xien, courtesy name Zhongfan, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner and was a son of Prince Rui Chunying.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，賜頭品頂戴，授頭等侍衛，乾清門行走。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he was granted the first-rank cap button, appointed first-rank guardsman, and permitted to attend at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 6 he received the first-rank cap button, became a first-class guardsman, and was granted attendance at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉御前侍衛，兼副都統、鑾儀使、上駟院卿，轉奉宸院卿，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to imperial bodyguard, concurrently served as vice president of the banner, Director of Imperial Ceremonial, and Director of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to Director of the Imperial Parks, and was moved to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he was promoted to imperial bodyguard and concurrently held posts as banner vice president, Director of Imperial Ceremonial, and Director of the Imperial Stud; he later headed the Imperial Parks and became grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授內務府大臣，調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of the Imperial Household and transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 20 he became Minister of the Imperial Household and was moved to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，仁宗崩於熱河避暑山莊，事出倉猝，禧恩以內廷扈從，建議宣宗有定亂勳，當繼位。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Emperor Renzong died at the Rehe summer resort; the affair arose in sudden haste; Xien, as an inner-court attendant, proposed that the Xuanzong Emperor had merit in quelling disorder and ought to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 Emperor Renzong died suddenly at the Rehe summer palace. Xien, attending within the palace, argued that the prince who would become Emperor Xuanzong had quelled the crisis and should take the throne.

sentences.zh: 樞臣托津、戴均元等猶豫，禧恩抗論，眾不能奪。

translations.literal: Grand councillors Tuojin, Dai Junyuan, and others hesitated; Xien argued forcefully and the assembly could not overrule him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councillors such as Tuojin and Dai Junyuan hesitated, but Xien pressed his case so firmly that none could gainsay him.

sentences.zh: 會得秘匱硃諭，乃偕諸臣奉宣宗即位，命在御前大臣、領侍衛大臣上行走。

translations.literal: When a vermilion edict was obtained from the secret casket, he together with the other ministers installed the Xuanzong Emperor on the throne and was ordered to attend above the ranks of imperial presence ministers and chief guards ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Once the vermilion edict was found in the secret casket, he and the other ministers enthroned Emperor Xuanzong and was ordered to walk in precedence above the imperial presence ministers and chief guards ministers.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，擢理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時哈薩克部眾潛聚烏梁海，議遷徙安置，增設卡倫。

translations.literal: At that time Kazakh tribesmen were secretly gathering at Wulianghai; relocation and settlement were discussed and additional barrier stations were to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Kazakh tribesmen were then gathering covertly at Wulianghai; the court debated resettling them and adding cordon stations.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書松筠諳習邊事，上每垂詢，禧恩因以諮之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Songyun was well versed in frontier affairs; the emperor often made inquiries, and Xien therefore consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Songyun knew frontier affairs well; the emperor often consulted him, and Xien sought his advice.

sentences.zh: 松筠素坦率，遂代刪改疏稿。

translations.literal: Songyun was by nature frank and forthright and thereupon revised the memorial draft on Xien's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Songyun was blunt by nature and took it upon himself to revise Xien's memorial draft.

sentences.zh: 禧恩怒，以上聞，松筠坐越職干預被譴。

translations.literal: Xien was angry and reported it to the emperor; Songyun was punished for overstepping his office and interfering.
translations.idiomatic: Xien was furious and reported the matter; Songyun was reprimanded for overstepping his authority.

sentences.zh: 尋調工部，仍兼署理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Works while still concurrently acting as Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Ministry of Works while continuing to act as Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 6 he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，加太子少保，署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given the honorary title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and served as acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 he received the honorary rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and acted as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，隨扈盛京，詔念睿親王多爾袞數定大勳，加恩後裔，賜禧恩雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Mukden; an edict recalled that Prince Rui Dorgon had several times secured great merit and extended grace to his descendants, granting Xien the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 he accompanied the emperor to Mukden. An edict honored Prince Rui Dorgon's great service and rewarded his descendants with the double-eyed peacock feather for Xien.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖南江華瑤趙金龍作亂，命禧恩偕盛京將軍瑚松額督師，未至，總督盧坤、提督羅思舉已平之，殲金龍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua in Hunan rebelled; Xien was ordered together with Mukden General Husong'e to command the army; before they arrived, Governor Lu Kun and Provincial Commander Luo Siju had already pacified it and destroyed Jinlong.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua, Hunan, rose in revolt. Xien was ordered to take command with Mukden general Husong'e, but before they arrived Governor Lu Kun and commander Luo Siju had already crushed the rebellion and killed Jinlong.

sentences.zh: 禧恩素貴倨，奉命視師，意氣甚盛，嗛諸將不待而告捷，謂金龍死未可信。

translations.literal: Xien had always been noble and arrogant; ordered to inspect the army, his spirit was very high; he resented that the generals reported victory without waiting for him and said Jinlong's death was not yet credible.
translations.idiomatic: Xien had long been proud and overbearing. Sent to take command, he arrived in high spirits, resented the generals' premature victory reports, and declared Jinlong's death unconfirmed.

sentences.zh: 思舉以金龍焚骸及佩物為證，議始息。

translations.literal: Siju produced Jinlong's burned remains and personal ornaments as proof, and the dispute then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Siju produced Jinlong's charred remains and personal effects as proof, and the dispute ended.

sentences.zh: 廣東瑤匪趙仔青竄入湖南，率提督餘步雲、總兵曾勝追剿之；

translations.literal: The Yao bandit Zhao Zaiqing of Guangdong fled into Hunan; he led Provincial Commander Yu Buyun and Regional Commander Zeng Sheng in pursuit and suppression;
translations.idiomatic: The Yao bandit Zhao Zaiqing fled from Guangdong into Hunan; Xien led commander Yu Buyun and regional commander Zeng Sheng in pursuit;

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫吳榮光疏陳善後事。

translations.literal: together with Governor Wu Rongguang he memorialized on matters of pacification and follow-up.
translations.idiomatic: and with Governor Wu Rongguang memorialized on post-conflict arrangements.

sentences.zh: 湖南既定，而兩廣總督李鴻賓剿連山瑤，閱半年，軍屢挫。

translations.literal: Hunan was settled, but Governor-General Li Hongbin of the Two Guangs was suppressing the Lianshan Yao; after half a year the army suffered repeated setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was pacified, but in Guangdong and Guangxi Governor-General Li Hongbin's campaign against the Lianshan Yao had stalled for half a year with repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 詔逮鴻賓，以禧恩署總督，由湖南進兵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Hongbin arrested; Xien was made acting governor-general and advanced troops from Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin was arrested and Xien made acting governor-general, advancing into Guangdong from Hunan.

sentences.zh: 遣步雲、勝等先後破賊，擒首逆鄧三、盤文理，毀其巢。

translations.literal: He sent Buyun, Sheng, and others in succession to defeat the bandits, capture the chief rebels Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroy their lairs.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Buyun, Sheng, and others to defeat the rebels in succession, capture the ringleaders Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroy their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，諸瑤乞降。

translations.literal: In only one month the various Yao groups begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the Yao groups surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其奏功迅速，賜三眼花翎，封不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: An edict praised his swift report of merit, granted the triple-eyed peacock feather, and enfeoffed him as Duke of the Second Rank not entering the eight shares.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his swift victory, granted the triple-eyed peacock feather, and enfeoffed him as Duke of the Second Rank outside the eight-share allotment.

sentences.zh: 班師，途次丁母憂，溫諭慰之。

translations.literal: On returning from campaign he encountered mourning for his mother en route; a warm edict consoled him.
translations.idiomatic: While returning from campaign he learned of his mother's death; the emperor sent a warm message of condolence.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孝慎皇后薨，命理喪儀，坐議禮徵引違制，褫御前大臣、戶部尚書、內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Empress Xiaoshen died; he was charged with arranging the funeral rites and, for citing regulations improperly in deliberating ritual, was stripped of the posts of imperial presence minister, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13, after Empress Xiaoshen died, he oversaw the funeral rites but was dismissed from his posts as imperial presence minister, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of the Imperial Household for improper ritual citations.

sentences.zh: 尋复授理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以生日受屬員饋送，為御史趙敦詩所劾，疏辯得直，敦詩坐譴。

translations.literal: For accepting gifts from subordinates on his birthday he was impeached by Censor Zhao Dunshi; he memorialized in defense and was vindicated, and Dunshi was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Dunshi impeached him for accepting birthday gifts from subordinates; Xien's defense was accepted and Zhao Dunshi was punished instead.

sentences.zh: 十四年，因相度龍泉峪萬年吉地，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, for surveying the auspicious eternal site at Longquanyu, he was given the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 14, for surveying the imperial burial site at Longquan Valley, he received the honorary rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 調兵部尚書，兼署禮部戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War and concurrently acted as Minister of Rites and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Minister of War and concurrently acted as Minister of Rites and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔以南苑牲畜不蕃，禧恩久管奉宸苑，廢弛疏懈，罷其兼領。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year an edict said that livestock in the Southern Park were not multiplying; Xien had long managed the Imperial Parks and had been negligent and remiss, and he was removed from concurrent charge.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 an edict noted declining livestock in the Southern Park; Xien, who had long managed the Imperial Parks, was blamed for negligence and stripped of that concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 尋得員司積弊狀，盡罷諸兼職，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward chronic abuses among the staff were discovered; all his concurrent posts were removed and he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic abuses among his staff soon came to light; he lost all concurrent posts and was demoted to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，署盛京將軍，授理籓院侍郎，留將軍署任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as acting General of Mukden, was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and retained the acting general's post.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 he acted as general of Mukden, was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and kept the acting generalship.

sentences.zh: 英吉利內犯，海疆戒嚴，命治盛京防務。

translations.literal: England invaded inland; the maritime frontier was placed on alert; he was ordered to manage Mukden's defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain invaded, the coast was placed on alert and he was ordered to organize Mukden's defenses.

sentences.zh: 既而和議成，疏陳善後十事，並巡洋章程，如議行。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he memorialized ten items for follow-up and regulations for coastal patrol, and these were implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made he memorialized ten postwar measures and coastal patrol regulations, which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以病解職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 he resigned due to illness.

sentences.zh: 坐失察內地民人越朝鮮界墾地，削公爵，降二等輔國將軍。

translations.literal: For failure to detect inland commoners crossing the Korean border to reclaim land, his ducal title was removed and he was demoted to General of the State of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his ducal title and was demoted to general of the state of the second rank for failing to stop Chinese settlers from farming across the Korean border.

sentences.zh: 三十年，起署馬蘭鎮總兵、密雲副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was recalled to serve as acting regional commander at Malan garrison and vice president at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 he was recalled to act as garrison commander at Malan and vice president at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，召授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 1 he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢戶部尚書，協辦大學士，管理籓院事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue, made Associate Grand Secretary, and charged with managing Court of Colonial Affairs affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he became Minister of Revenue, Associate Grand Secretary, and superintendent of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保，諡文莊。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 禧恩自道光初被恩眷，及孝全皇后被選入宮，家故寒素，賴其資助，遂益用事。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Daoguang Xien enjoyed imperial favor; when Empress Xiaoquan was selected to enter the palace, her family had been poor and relied on his financial support, and he therefore wielded power ever more.
translations.idiomatic: From early Daoguang Xien enjoyed the emperor's favor. When Empress Xiaoquan entered the palace, her impoverished family relied on his support, and his influence grew accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遍膺禁近要職，兼攝諸部，凌轢同列，人皆側目。

translations.literal: He held important posts throughout the inner court, concurrently directed many ministries, bullied his colleagues, and everyone looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: He held one inner-court post after another, headed multiple ministries concurrently, bullied colleagues, and drew wary glances from all sides.

sentences.zh: 後晚寵衰，禧恩亦數獲譴罷斥。

translations.literal: Later, as favor waned in his old age, Xien also repeatedly suffered reprimands and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial favor waned in his later years, Xien was repeatedly reprimanded and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，乃復起，不兩年登協揆焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne he was raised up again, and in less than two years reached the associate grand secretary rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne he was restored to office and within two years reached the associate grand secretary rank.

sentences.zh: 陳官俊，字偉堂，山東濰縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Guanjun, styled Weitang, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guanjun, courtesy name Weitang, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷贊善。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and moved to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Jiaqing 13, entered the Hanlin as a probationer academician, became a compiler, and was promoted tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，入直上書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he entered the Imperial Lecture Hall on permanent duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 21 he was assigned to regular duty in the Imperial Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢洗馬，累遷右庶子。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he placed second class, was promoted to Keeper of the Stud, and rose in succession to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Placing second class in the grand examination, he was promoted to Keeper of the Stud and later to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and supervised as educational commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and served as educational commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，命各省明定陋規，中外臣工多言窒礙，官俊亦疏陳不可行，詔嘉之，予議敘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang an order went out for each province to define clearly improper customary fees; ministers at court and abroad mostly said this would cause obstruction, and Guanjun also memorialized that it was unworkable; an edict praised this and granted him consideration for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 the court ordered provinces to define improper customary fees clearly. Most officials warned the policy would cause gridlock; Guanjun agreed in a memorial. The emperor praised him and granted consideration for promotion.

sentences.zh: 會密諭留心察訪官吏賢否、政治得失，官俊恃曾直內廷為宣宗所眷，意氣甚張。

translations.literal: At the same time a secret edict instructed attention to investigating whether officials were worthy and the gains and losses of government; Guanjun relied on having once served in the inner court and being favored by the Xuanzong Emperor, and his spirit was very overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict then instructed officials to report on merit and misconduct in government. Guanjun, trusting his former inner-court service and the emperor's favor, grew swaggering in manner.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍講學士，命回京，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was moved to Reader of the Hanlin Academy, ordered to return to the capital, and still served in the Imperial Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin reader, recalled to the capital, and continued in the Imperial Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫成格追劾官俊在學政任毆差買妾，妄作威福，大開奔競。

translations.literal: Shanxi Governor Cheng Ge pursued impeachment of Guanjun for beating runners and buying a concubine during his term as educational commissioner, arrogantly wielding power, and greatly opening the door to factional scrambling.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi governor Cheng Ge impeached Guanjun for beating runners, buying a concubine, abusing his authority as educational commissioner, and encouraging corrupt patronage.

sentences.zh: 上以官俊於毆差買妾已自承不諱，曾薦舉魏元烺、邱鳴泰，人材尚不繆；

translations.literal: The emperor held that Guanjun had already confessed without concealment to beating runners and buying a concubine, and had once recommended Wei Yuanliang and Qiu Mingtai—his judgment of talent was not mistaken;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Guanjun had confessed to beating runners and buying a concubine, and that his recommendations of Wei Yuanliang and Qiu Mingtai showed sound judgment;

sentences.zh: 惟所述太監往河東查訪鹽務控案，事出無稽，解職就質，命長齡道出山西，傳旨面詰成格，亦以不能指實引咎，遂兩斥之。

translations.literal: only the account of eunuchs going to Hedong to investigate salt administration accusations was groundless; he was removed from office to stand trial; Changling was ordered to pass through Shanxi en route and transmit an edict to question Cheng Ge in person; Cheng Ge also could not substantiate his charges and accepted blame, and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: but his claim that eunuchs had been sent to Hedong to investigate salt affairs was unfounded. Guanjun was removed pending trial; Changling was ordered through Shanxi to question Cheng Ge in person. Cheng Ge could not substantiate his charges and accepted blame, and both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 官俊降編修，罷直上書房。

translations.literal: Guanjun was demoted to compiler and removed from the Imperial Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun was demoted to compiler and stripped of his Lecture Hall post.

sentences.zh: 連典貴州、江西鄉試，歷中允、祭酒、侍講學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He presided in succession over the Guizhou and Jiangxi provincial examinations, and served as middle secretary, Chancellor of the National University, Reader of the Hanlin Academy, and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Guizhou and Jiangxi provincial examinations in succession and held posts as middle secretary, chancellor of the National University, Hanlin reader, and grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授禮部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 16 he became Vice Minister of Rites and was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 東陵郎中慶玉侵帑籍沒，主事全孚預告，多所寄頓。

translations.literal: Director Qing Yu of the Eastern Tombs embezzled treasury funds and was confiscated; Secretary Quan Fu had given advance warning and deposited much property elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Director Qing Yu of the Eastern Tombs embezzled treasury funds and was confiscated; secretary Quan Fu had warned him in advance and helped him hide assets.

sentences.zh: 事覺，語由官俊閒談漏洩，回奏复諱飾，詔斥失大臣體，褫職。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, word had leaked through Guanjun's casual conversation; in his reply memorial he again concealed the facts; an edict denounced his loss of a grand minister's bearing and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: When the case surfaced, word had leaked through Guanjun's idle talk; he concealed the facts in his memorial reply. An edict condemned his unbecoming conduct and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起為通政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 he was recalled as commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部侍郎，管理三庫。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Minister of Personnel and managed the Three Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Minister of Personnel and managed the Three Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as Minister of Personnel, he was made Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 he became Associate Grand Secretary while serving as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 官俊再起，歷典鄉會試、殿廷禦試，每與衡校。

translations.literal: Guanjun rose again and presided in succession over provincial examinations, metropolitan examinations, and palace imperial examinations, each time participating in grading.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to office, Guanjun presided over provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations and took part in grading each time.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He served as chief tutor of the Imperial Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief tutor of the Imperial Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 編修童福承素無行，直上書房授皇子讀。

translations.literal: Compiler Tong Fucheng had always been without proper conduct yet taught the princes in the Imperial Lecture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Tong Fucheng, a man of poor character, nevertheless taught the princes in the Imperial Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳壇劾之，語及福承為官俊妻作祭文，措詞過當。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Tan impeached him, mentioning that Fucheng had composed a funeral elegy for Guanjun's wife with excessive wording.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Chen Tan impeached him, noting that Fucheng had written an elegy for Guanjun's wife in overwrought language.

sentences.zh: 福承譴黜，詔斥官俊容隱不奏，罷總師傅，議降三級調用，從寬留任。

translations.literal: Fucheng was reprimanded and dismissed; an edict denounced Guanjun for concealing the matter and not reporting it, removed him as chief tutor, proposed demotion three ranks and transfer, but leniently allowed him to remain in post.
translations.idiomatic: Fucheng was dismissed. An edict rebuked Guanjun for covering up the matter, stripped him of the chief tutorship, and proposed demoting him three ranks—but allowed him to remain in office as a leniency.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，優詔賜卹，稱其心田坦白，贈太子太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文愨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; a favorable edict granted condolence payments, praised his open-heartedness, posthumously gave him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave the posthumous title Wenque.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 29. A gracious edict granted funeral honors, praised his open-hearted character, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave him the posthumous name Wenque.

sentences.zh: 賜其孫厚鍾、厚滋並為舉人。

translations.literal: His grandsons Houzhong and Houzi were both granted the juren degree.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Houzhong and Houzi were both granted juren degrees.

sentences.zh: 官俊初直上書房，授宣宗長子奕緯讀，宣宗嘉其訓迪有方。

translations.literal: Guanjun first served in the Imperial Lecture Hall teaching the Xuanzong Emperor's eldest son Yizhi; the Xuanzong Emperor praised his effective instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun first taught the future Emperor Xuanzong's eldest son Yizhi in the Imperial Lecture Hall, and the emperor praised his instruction.

sentences.zh: 後皇長子逾冠而薨，上深以為恫，故遇官俊特厚，屢獲咎而恩禮始終不衰。

translations.literal: Later the eldest imperial son passed the capping age and died; the emperor was deeply grieved, and therefore treated Guanjun with special favor; though he repeatedly incurred blame, imperial grace and courtesy never waned.
translations.idiomatic: When the eldest prince died after coming of age, the emperor was deeply grieved and treated Guanjun with special favor; despite repeated punishments, imperial grace never faded.

sentences.zh: 子介祺，道光二十五年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Jieqi passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang and served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jieqi took his jinshi degree in Daoguang 25 and served as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，助軍餉，加侍講學士銜。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng he contributed military funds and was given the honorary rank of Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign he contributed military funds and received the honorary rank of Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 後在籍治團練，守城，賑饑，賜二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Later while at home he organized militia training, defended the city, and relieved famine; he was granted the second-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while at home, he organized militia, defended the city, and relieved famine, and was granted the second-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 介祺績學好古，所藏鐘鼎、彝器、金石為近代之冠。

translations.literal: Jieqi was learned and fond of antiquity; his collection of bells, tripods, ritual vessels, and bronze and stone inscriptions was the finest of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Jieqi was a serious scholar of antiquity; his collection of bronzes and stone inscriptions was unrivaled in his day.

sentences.zh: 卓秉恬，字靜遠，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Zhuo Bingtian, styled Jingyuan, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Bingtian, courtesy name Jingyuan, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，年甫逾冠，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, had just passed the capping age, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Jiaqing 7, entered the Hanlin as a probationer academician while still barely past his capping year, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改御史，歷給事中，章疏凡數十上。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to censor, served successively as supervising secretary, and submitted several dozen memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 he became a censor, later a supervising secretary, and submitted dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 論盜風未息，由捕役與盜賊因緣為奸，捕役藉盜賊以漁利，盜賊仗捕役為護符，民間控告，官不為理，盜賊結恨，又召荼毒；

translations.literal: He discussed how banditry had not ceased because constables and bandits colluded by circumstance—constables used bandits to fish for profit, bandits relied on constables as protective talismans, when the people lodged complaints officials would not act, bandits nursed resentment, and further calamity was invited;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that banditry persisted because constables and thieves colluded: constables profited from thieves, thieves used constables as protection, officials ignored civilian complaints, and resentment bred further violence;

sentences.zh: 直隸之大名、滄州，河南之衛輝、陳州、山東之曹州、東昌、武定，江甦之徐州最甚，請飭實力禁懲。

translations.literal: it was worst in Daming and Cangzhou in Zhili, Weihui and Chenzhou in Henan, Caozhou, Dongchang, and Wuding in Shandong, and Xuzhou in Jiangsu; he requested stern prohibition and punishment in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: the worst areas were Daming and Cangzhou in Zhili, Weihui and Chenzhou in Henan, Caozhou, Dongchang, and Wuding in Shandong, and Xuzhou in Jiangsu; he urged strict enforcement and punishment.

sentences.zh: 巡漕山東，履勘泰安、兗州各屬，探濬新泉四十三處，定名勒石。

translations.literal: On grain-transport patrol in Shandong he personally surveyed the jurisdictions of Tai'an and Yanzhou, explored and dredged forty-three new springs, fixed their names, and carved them on stone.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting grain transport in Shandong he surveyed Tai'an and Yanzhou, located and dredged forty-three new springs, and recorded their names on stone steles.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺少卿、順天府丞。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice President of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Assistant Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice President of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and assistant prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，疏言：「由陝西略陽迄東至湖北鄖西，謂之南山老林；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized: "From Lueyang in Shaanxi eastward to Yunxi in Hubei is called the Old Forest of the Southern Mountains;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 he memorialized: "From Lueyang in Shaanxi east to Yunxi in Hubei lies what is called the Old Forest of the Southern Mountains;

sentences.zh: 由陝西寧羌迄南而東，經四川境至湖北保康，謂之巴山老林。

translations.literal: from Ningqiang in Shaanxi south and east, passing through Sichuan to Baokang in Hubei, is called the Old Forest of the Ba Mountains."
translations.idiomatic: from Ningqiang in Shaanxi south and east through Sichuan to Baokang in Hubei is called the Old Forest of the Ba Mountains."

sentences.zh: 地皆磽瘠，糧徭極微。

translations.literal: The land was all barren and poor, and grain levies and corvée were extremely light.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was poor and barren, and grain levies and labor obligations were minimal.

sentences.zh: 無業遊民，給地主錢數千，即租種數溝數嶺。

translations.literal: Idle wanderers without occupation gave landowners several thousand cash and then rented several ravines and ridges to cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: Landless drifters paid landowners a few thousand cash and rented whole ravines and ridges to farm.

sentences.zh: 歲薄不收則徙去，謂之棚民。

translations.literal: If the year's harvest was poor they moved away; they were called shed people.
translations.idiomatic: When harvests failed they moved on; they were known as shed dwellers.

sentences.zh: 良莠莫辨，攘奪時聞。

translations.literal: Good and bad could not be distinguished, and plunder was heard of from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Good and bad elements were indistinguishable, and robbery was common.

sentences.zh: 一遇旱澇，一二奸民為之倡，即蟻附蜂起。

translations.literal: Whenever drought or flood occurred, one or two wicked commoners took the lead and people swarmed like ants and bees.
translations.idiomatic: In drought or flood, a few ringleaders could set off mass uprisings overnight.

sentences.zh: 州縣以地方遼闊，莫能追捕，遂至互相容隱。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, because the territory was vast, could not pursue and capture them, and thus came to conceal one another's failures.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties, unable to police such vast territory, often covered for one another instead of pursuing offenders.

sentences.zh: 迨釀成大案，即加參劾，事已無濟。

translations.literal: Only when a major case had brewed were impeachments added, and by then nothing could be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachments came only after major outbreaks, when it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 且事連三省，大吏往返諮商，州縣奉文辦理，恆在數月之後。

translations.literal: Moreover the affair involved three provinces; high officials went back and forth in consultation, and when prefectures and counties received documents to act, it was always months later.
translations.idiomatic: Because cases spanned three provinces, senior officials exchanged memos while local officials often received orders months too late.

sentences.zh: 與其即一隅而專謀之，何如合三省而共議之。

translations.literal: Rather than planning for one corner alone, how much better to unite the three provinces in joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than treating each district in isolation, the three provinces should deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 請於扼要之地，專設大員控制。

translations.literal: He requested that at a strategic point a dedicated high official be specially appointed to exercise control.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed posting a senior official at a strategic point with sole authority over the region.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗深韙之，詔下三省會議，未果行，僅將邊境文武酌就要地改駐添設。

translations.literal: " The Xuanzong Emperor deeply approved; an edict was sent down for the three provinces to confer, but it was not carried out; only frontier civil and military officials were suitably relocated or added at key points.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanzong strongly approved. An edict ordered the three provinces to confer, but the full plan was never implemented; only some frontier posts were relocated or reinforced.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，調奉天府丞，丁父憂去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Assistant Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture and left office on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 he became assistant prefect of Shuntian and resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，歷太僕寺、大理寺少卿，太僕寺卿，宗人府丞，內閣學士，典江南鄉試。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served successively as Vice President of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review, President of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination.
