translations.idiomatic: After mourning he held posts as vice president and president of the Court of the Imperial Stud, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and grand secretary, and presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷禮部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was moved to Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15 he became Vice Minister of Rites and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He supervised as educational commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史，召還京，兼管順天府尹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, recalled to the capital, and concurrently managed the affairs of the Shuntian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, he was recalled to Beijing and concurrently managed Shuntian prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、戶部、吏部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of War, Minister of Revenue, Minister of Personnel, and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of War, Minister of Revenue, Minister of Personnel, and Associate Grand Secretary in succession.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜文淵閣大學士，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity and advanced to the Hall of Military Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 he became Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity and was advanced to the Hall of Military Eminence.

sentences.zh: 歷管兵部、戶部、工部，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He successively managed the Ministries of War, Revenue, and Works and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He headed the Ministries of War, Revenue, and Works in turn and was granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，卒，年七十四，贈太子太保，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he died, aged seventy-four; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianfeng 5 at the age of seventy-four and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 秉恬兼管京尹最久，凡十有八年。

translations.literal: Bingtian concurrently managed the capital prefect the longest, altogether eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian held concurrent charge of the capital prefecture longer than anyone else—a total of eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 時九卿會議，一二王公樞相主之，餘率佔位畫諾。

translations.literal: At that time in conferences of the Nine Ministers, one or two princes and grand councillors presided, and the rest generally occupied seats and marked approval.
translations.idiomatic: At Nine Ministers' conferences, one or two princes or grand councillors dominated while the rest merely nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 秉恬在列，時有辯論，不為用事者所喜。

translations.literal: Bingtian was among them and from time to time argued; he was not liked by those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian often spoke up in debate, which displeased those in power.

sentences.zh: 子枟，道光二十年進士，官至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Ting passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Daoguang and rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ting took his jinshi degree in Daoguang 20 and rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自設軍機處，閣臣不預樞務。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Since the Grand Council was established, grand secretaries did not participate in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: After the Grand Council was established, grand secretaries no longer took part in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 始猶取名德較著者表望中朝，繼則旅進旅退之流，且以年資眷睞，馴躋鼎鉉矣。

translations.literal: At first men of rather notable reputation and virtue were still chosen to display prestige at court; later came the sort who advanced and retired in groups, and even by seniority and imperial favor docilely climbed to the highest ministerial seats.
translations.idiomatic: At first men of real reputation still lent dignity to the court; later the posts went to men who rose by seniority and favor, docilely filling the highest seats.

sentences.zh: 寶興號嫺吏事，而蒙簠簋不飭之聲；

translations.literal: Bao Xing was said to be skilled in administrative affairs, yet bore the reputation of laxity in ritual vessels;
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xing was considered skilled in administration, yet bore a reputation for personal laxity;

sentences.zh: 敬徵數視河工，差著勞勚；

translations.literal: Jingzheng repeatedly inspected river works and showed some merit in labor;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzheng inspected river works repeatedly and earned some credit for his labors;

sentences.zh: 禧恩、陳官俊並恃恩私，崛而復起；

translations.literal: Xien and Chen Guanjun both relied on private favor and rose again after setbacks;
translations.idiomatic: Xien and Chen Guanjun both relied on private favor to rise again after falls;

sentences.zh: 卓秉恬以言官進，視緘默自安者稍表異焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo Bingtian advanced as a censorial official and showed somewhat more distinction than those who kept silent for their own comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Bingtian entered through the censorate and stood out slightly from officials who kept silent for safety.
